events.title: Google Chrome 1.0 released
events.summary: Google launched Chrome in beta on September 2, 2008 — a minimalist browser built on WebKit with a multi-process architecture and the new V8 JavaScript engine.
events.about: Chrome treated each tab as a separate process for stability, shipped a blazing-fast JS VM (V8), and popularized the omnibox address bar. It quickly overtook Firefox and IE, drove the shift to evergreen auto-updates, and later forked WebKit into Blink — defining how modern browsers are built.

narrative.whyChosen: Chrome reset performance expectations and became the world's most-used browser.
narrative.whyImportant: V8, multi-process tabs, and rapid releases became the template every competitor followed.
narrative.problemSolved: Web apps like Gmail and Maps were pushing browsers to their limits; Google needed a platform built for applications, not just documents.
